name: Product mockups and artwork
summary: Turns finished artwork into product mockups on the store listing. The agent makes the mockups; the crons read the store's products and queue the listing update for a person to approve. Crons read and queue only.

covered_by.mockup-build: skill (agent builds the mockups in Figma, outside the kit)

crons.name: catalogue
crons.summary: Read the store's products, record which have no images, and report which approved mockups are now live.

crons.name: listing
crons.summary: Queue the listing update for each mockup set the agent has written, for a person to approve.

draft_ops_note: The only draft operation is a read of the store's products. Adding images to a product changes what customers see on the store, so it is a live operation and a cron can only queue it.

woocommerce.covers: read the store's products page by page; batch-update product images (queued for approval only)

gaps: Figma: no kit platform. The mockups are built and exported outside the kit, to an https location the business controls, then written to the mockups record.

Needs core: an approved listing update replays the images array built when it was queued. An image added or removed on the live product between queue and approval is dropped on approval. Fix: the runtime re-plans a live act from current product data at approval, or refuses to run when the product changed since it was queued.

Shopify: product media operations are mapped (productCreateMedia, productUpdateMedia, productReorderMedia, productVariantAppendMedia) but index-only: no argument mapping, and the endpoint map holds only doc URLs, so no field names can be confirmed. No Shopify adapter yet.
WooCommerce reads: docs.get_products is read page by page (page and per_page, 100 a page, at most 20 pages, so 2,000 products). A store with more products than that is read only up to the cap.
WooCommerce batch update replaces the images array it is given. The adapter keeps existing images by id and appends the new ones, so nothing already live is dropped.
No command writes a mockups record yet. The CRM shell or a CLI must add one; core/ is not edited here.
Mockup design, artwork checks and print prep (bleed, dielines, colour profile) are judgment steps for the agent and the owner. The platform docs do not cover print prep.
Confirm the workflow steps and platform coverage with the business before enabling its crons.
Figma's proof-sent, approval and revise steps are not covered by the mapped docs; the owner's sign-off happens in the CRM shell approval.
